The current_key_sha256 field is a convenience digest of the base64-encoded key string, not an independent trust anchor — do not use it as your sole verification reference.' findings.claim: CG-R2-001 carry-forward: WP-SCP-021 §13 unknowns U-21-b, U-21-e, U-21-h still have no closure documentation three rounds after the implementation that resolves them. No Resolution column, no inline note, no separate closure doc.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-021-scp-as-mcp-server.md:241-253: table header '| ID | Question | Closes before |' — original three-column format unchanged. U-21-b (line 246), U-21-e (line 249), U-21-h (line 252) retain original row text. No docs/reviews/WP-SCP-021/unknowns-closure.md or equivalent found. Implementation state: subscribe=True capability wired in register_resources (U-21-b, verified by test_resource_notifications.py); direct scp://rules/registry exposed without facade (U-21-e); domain-map derived from registry in _build_domain_map lines 673-709 (U-21-h) — none traceable to a documented decision.
findings.impact: Three load-bearing design decisions have no ADR-level traceability. U-21-b is operationally critical for 021F adopter hooks: without a recorded client-support matrix documenting which MCP clients support resource-update notifications vs. require re-polling fallback, adopters cannot safely implement the fallback path. The 021F reviewer has no governance checkpoint to verify these were consciously resolved rather than accidentally implemented.
findings.mitigation: Update WP-SCP-021 §13 by appending a Resolution column to the table. U-21-b: 'FastMCP subscribe=True capability wired in register_resources; test_resource_notifications.py verifies notification delivery; Claude Code / Desktop / Codex client matrix validation deferred to 021F adopter guide; re-polling fallback required for non-subscribing clients.' U-21-e: 'Direct exposure accepted; facade deferred pending registry schema-version stability review in 021E/021F.' U-21-h: 'Derived from registry applies_to fields in _build_domain_map; separate authoring rejected.' No code change required.

findings.claim: CG-R2-002 carry-forward: server.py instructions field still reads 'Tools and resources are introduced in later implementation slices.' — contradicting the fully registered 021D server, unchanged after three fix rounds.
findings.evidence: server.py:44-47: instructions: str = ('Standards Control Plane MCP scaffold. Tools and resources are introduced ' 'in later implementation slices.'). ScpMcpServer.__post_init__ lines 57-61 calls register_tools and register_resources unconditionally. Class docstring (line 41) was updated in fr1 to 'Stdio MCP server scaffold with tools and resources registered.' but the MCP-protocol-visible instructions field was not touched. No test file asserts ScpMcpServer().instructions content. Grep for 'in later implementation slices' confirms stale text is live in the current HEAD.
findings.impact: Every MCP client connecting to the live server — Claude Code, Codex, cursor — receives an instructions string stating the server has no current tools or resources. This is a public API contract breach contradicting registered capabilities. An adopter reading instructions as part of discovery would conclude the server is a placeholder and bypass it. The mismatch undermines governance completeness for any external reviewer of the 021D slice.
findings.mitigation: Update server.py:44-47 instructions field: 'Standards Control Plane MCP server. Resources: scp://rules/registry, scp://rules/domain-map, scp://decisions, scp://findings/open, scp://waivers, scp://status, scp://security/signing-keys, plus per-ID templates (scp://rule/{rule_id}, scp://waiver/{waiver_id}, scp://finding/{finding_id}, scp://decision/{decision_id}). Seven governance tools registered.' Add a test asserting 'scp://rules/registry' in ScpMcpServer().instructions to prevent future drift.

findings.claim: CG-R2-003 carry-forward: 'referencing' imported directly in test_resource_schemas.py but not declared in pyproject.toml; jsonschema declared as a runtime dependency when only test code uses it.
findings.evidence: test_resource_schemas.py:7: 'from referencing import Registry, Resource'. pyproject.toml: 'referencing' absent; jsonschema>=4.25.0 in [project.dependencies] (runtime). referencing is a hard dep of jsonschema 4.x and thus transitively available, but strict resolvers (uv, pip-compile) may not surface transitive deps. No production module imports jsonschema directly.
findings.impact: CI environments using strict dependency isolation or --no-deps installs may fail to import referencing. Treating jsonschema as a runtime dep conflates runtime and test dependency surfaces.
findings.mitigation: Add 'referencing>=0.30' to [project.optional-dependencies] dev list. If no production code imports jsonschema directly, move it from [project.dependencies] to the dev optional-dependencies list.

findings.claim: CG-R2-004 carry-forward: no tracked-forward item in WP-SCP-021 §4 AC list or 021F dispatch plan for the 021F adopter guide obligation to include a signing-keys transport-trust warning. R1 SB-MAJ-001 residual remains untracked.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-021 §4 acceptance criteria and §9: no entry named 'signing-keys-adopter-warning' or equivalent. R1 SB-MAJ-001 mitigation explicitly required: 'the 021F adopter guide must contain an explicit warning that scp://security/signing-keys is transport-trust-dependent and must be backed by the committed-file fallback.' The trust_model.adopter_requirement field communicates the requirement programmatically, but there is no governance checkpoint ensuring a human-readable warning appears in 021F documentation. Carrying forward for a third time.
findings.impact: Adopters implementing 021F integrations without an explicit adopter-guide warning may configure hooks that exclusively trust the MCP-delivered signing key without cross-checking the committed keyring. The 021F reviewer has no visible obligation to verify the warning's presence, so the SB-MAJ-001 attack surface can re-open silently at 021F.
findings.mitigation: Add named tracked-forward item to WP-SCP-021 §4 or 021F dispatch plan: 'signing-keys-adopter-warning: adopter guide must state scp://security/signing-keys is transport-trust-dependent; hooks must cross-check current_key.public_key against docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub committed file before accepting any verification result.' No code change required.

findings.claim: CG-R2-005 carry-forward: test_resource_schemas.py reads schemas via CWD-relative Path('schemas/scp_mcp') — fails when pytest is invoked from any directory other than the project root.
findings.evidence: test_resource_schemas.py:15: schema_root = Path('schemas/scp_mcp'); line 25: Path('schemas/scp_mcp') / name. Both resolve relative to CWD. pyproject.toml testpaths=['tests'] does not fix CWD. Developer running 'pytest tests/scp_mcp/test_resources/test_resource_schemas.py' from within tests/ gets FileNotFoundError masking the root cause.
findings.mitigation: Replace CWD-relative paths with file-relative: schema_root = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent.parent / 'schemas' / 'scp_mcp'.

Asserts schema_version='1.0.0', key_id='scp-mcp-2026-04', status dict with all five fields (last_updated='2026-04-29', current_branch, current_work_package, current_state, summary list), and recent_wp_merges filtered to the single WP-SCP-022 commit. resources.py:541-546: signing_keys_text = _read_committed_text(..., 'docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub') and signing_keys_body = _parse_signing_keys(signing_keys_text) — both called without any try/except inside _build_snapshot. _parse_signing_keys raises RuntimeError at lines 254-255 (multiple current keys) and lines 257-261 (no current key). No isolation block was added. The new test test_signing_keys_require_exactly_one_current_marker (test_signing_keys.py:32-51) asserts catalog.read_static('scp://security/signing-keys') raises RuntimeError('no current signing key declared') — it only calls the signing-keys URI and does not verify that scp://decisions or scp://waivers remain operational when signing keys fails. The test is consistent with both total-outage and isolated-error behavior; it does not close the DoS risk.
